category: Shipped scripts, projects and design blocks
description: Ready-made material installed with EAGLE 9.6.0 under <EAGLE>\examples: the editor scripts (.scr) in scripts\examples, the example projects in projects\examples (Arduino, BeagleBone, Seeed, TI LaunchPad, Nordic, hexapod, BGA, single-sided autorouting, tutorial and electrical-schematic files) and the design blocks (.dbl) in design blocks\examples (Adafruit, SparkFun, Nordic, timers, USB-to-UART, regulators, amplifiers, ESP8266 and small helper circuits). Installed examples open read-only; copy them to a project folder before editing. Apart from the two binary Grove-Button files, the .sch/.brd/.dbl files are XML and can also be read without EAGLE, and boards can be processed headless with eaglecon.

tools.name: eagle.scr
tools.description: The configuration script EAGLE runs automatically each time a drawing is loaded into an editor window (or the drawing type changes in a library), if it is found in the project directory or the script path. Sections labelled BRD:, SCH:, LBR:, DEV:, SYM: and PAC: apply settings per editor type; the shipped version calls default-assign.scr, defines the board layer presets Preset_Top, Preset_Bottom and Preset_Standard with DISPLAY = '...', sets grids and default widths/sizes, and adds MENU entries for designlink-order.ulp, pcb-service.ulp and the PADS package import ULP.
tools.usage: Runs automatically when a drawing is loaded (not with eagle -C); manually: SCRIPT eagle.scr
tools.notes: Preset layer groups can only be edited, renamed or removed here, not inside the editor. For personal settings put your own eagle.scr in the project directory or in a script directory (Options > Directories > Scripts).

tools.name: default-assign.scr
tools.description: Default keyboard shortcut assignments called from eagle.scr: general keys such as Ctrl+M MOVE, Ctrl+Z UNDO, Ctrl+Y REDO, Ctrl+Shift+A ADD, Ctrl+D DELETE, Ctrl+W WIRE, Ctrl+I INFO, Ctrl+F find.ulp, Ctrl+G NEWGROUP, and board keys for ERRORS, DRC, VALUE, RIPUP, HOLE and routing obstacle modes (Alt+G ignore, Alt+P push, Alt+W walkaround) and via patterns. Edit a copy to change or add shortcuts.
tools.usage: SCRIPT default-assign.scr   (or keep the SCRIPT line in eagle.scr)
tools.notes: Several further ASSIGN lines are commented out (# ...) and can be enabled.

tools.name: defaultcolors.scr
tools.description: Defines the colours of all three palettes (black, white and coloured background) with SET PALETTE <index> <ARGB hex>, including highlight colours and the colour groups. Use it to restore EAGLE's current default colours.
tools.notes: exp-palette.ulp exports your own palette in the same form.

tools.name: legacycolors.scr
tools.description: The legacy default-colours script: sets all palettes to the legacy default colours and also sets the layer palette assignments and fill styles back to their legacy values. Use it if you prefer the old colour scheme.
tools.notes: Revert with SCRIPT defaultcolors.scr.

tools.name: mylayers.scr
tools.description: Template for a personal layer scheme: sets colours and fill styles of all layers with SET COLOR_LAYER and SET FILL_LAYER and shows how SET USED_LAYERS limits the layers offered in the DISPLAY menu. Copy and edit it to define your own colours.
tools.notes: Edit a copy rather than the installed file.

tools.name: fill.scr and nofill.scr
tools.description: Two tiny scripts that switch the fill style of the Top, Bottom, tPlace and bPlace layers: fill.scr sets them solid with Display_Mode Real, nofill.scr sets them empty with Display_Mode NoDrill, which helps to inspect overlapping copper. They illustrate SET FILL_LAYER and SET DISPLAY_MODE.
tools.notes: Examples of defining your own fill styles.

tools.name: euro.scr
tools.description: Draws the outline of a Euro-format board (100 mm x 160 mm) in layer Dimension and corner markings in Top and Bottom, using a 1 mm grid, then zooms to fit. A compact example of drawing geometry with a script.
tools.notes: Adapt the coordinates for other board sizes.

tools.name: delete-signals.scr
tools.description: Removes all traces and airwires from a layout: it rips up everything, groups the whole area and deletes, then restores the previous layer display. It replaces the former DELETE SIGNALS command (written for EAGLE 5).
tools.notes: Destructive: save first. After it, a netlist can be re-read, e.g. from EXPORT NETSCRIPT.

tools.name: menu.scr
tools.description: Shows how to build a text command menu with submenus and aliases using MENU: a Grid menu with metric/imperial fine/coarse entries, a Display menu with top/bottom/placement views, a separator and plain commands (Add, Delete, Move, Edit, Quit). The same technique can put frequently used commands and ULPs into a menu.
tools.usage: SCRIPT menu.scr   (enable Options > User Interface > Command texts to see the menu)
tools.example: MENU 'Grid { Metric { Fine : Grid mm 0.1; | Coarse : Grid mm 1; } | On : Grid On; | Off : Grid Off; }' '---' 'Fit : Window Fit;';
tools.notes: The same MENU syntax is used in eagle.scr for the ULP menu entries.

tools.name: lbr-assign.scr
tools.description: Assigns keys in the Library Editor to library-editing ULPs and commands: next/previous device, symbol, package or library (editnext-*/editprev-*), description editors (nextdevdescript, nextpacdescript ...), rename and remove of the current object, save with WRITE, and edit-used-dev-pac-sym; in PAC and SYM mode keys place >NAME/>VALUE texts with standard layer and size. Commented lines show key bindings for sheet navigation and cam2printer/cam2dxf.
tools.usage: SCRIPT lbr-assign.scr   (or call it from eagle.scr)
tools.notes: Some comments in the script name different keys than the ASSIGN lines; the ASSIGN lines are authoritative.

tools.name: elektro-init.scr
tools.description: German-commented presets for electrical wiring diagrams, run from the Schematic Editor: 0.1 inch line grid with 0.01 inch alternate grid, AUTO_JUNCTION off, WIRE_BEND 2, and a Tools text menu for e-attributverwaltung.ulp, e-brueckenverwaltung.ulp and e-klemmenplan.ulp. Start it from the Schematic Editor, as its comments instruct.
tools.notes: Pairs with the elektro libraries and the e-*.ulp programs.

tools.name: Arduino Mega 2560 reference design
tools.description: Schematic and 2-layer board of the Arduino Mega 2560 reference board (ATmega2560, 54 digital I/O of which 14 PWM, 16 analog inputs, 4 UARTs, 16 MHz crystal, USB, power jack, ICSP header, reset button), with about 115 schematic parts and 72 board elements. It is a realistic mid-size design for trying CAM jobs, BOM export and ULPs.
tools.notes: Saved with EAGLE 7.1.2. The example command was checked on 9.6.0 without signing in (September 2026): it writes Gerber files, the Gerber job file, drill_1_16.xln and assembly/pick-and-place files under <out>\CAMOutputs. The -o directory must already exist (otherwise 'Output dir doesn't exist') and should be absolute; with a relative -o the drill file landed in a nested out\out folder.

tools.name: BeagleBone Blue and BeagleBone Black Wireless designs
tools.description: Two complete open-hardware single-board computers as consistent schematic/board pairs, each also in a _3D version with 3D packages assigned (added in 9.3.1): BeagleBone_Blue (about 300 elements, 4 copper layers with layer setup (1+2*15+16)) and BeagleBone_Black_Wireless (about 275 elements, 6 copper layers). Both are licensed CC-BY-4.0 (LICENSE.txt: Octavo Systems for Blue, GHI Electronics for Wireless).
tools.example: OPEN BeagleBone_Blue_3D.brd   # then FUSIONSYNC or view the 3D packages of the parts
tools.notes: Good test cases for multilayer CAM jobs (example_4_layer.cam, example_6_layer.cam).

tools.name: Seeed example projects
tools.description: Ten Seeed Studio designs as schematic/board pairs: Base-Shield-V2, CAN-BUS-Shield-v1.2, GPRS-Shield-V3.0, Grove-Button-v1.0, Grove-Relay (v1.2), Seeeduino-Stalker-v3.0, Seeeduino-v4.2, and Xadow-Basic-Sensors-v1.0, Xadow-GPS-v2 and Xadow-NFC-v2 (the Xadow folders also contain PDF prints). The library data is embedded in the files (e.g. libraries named Discrete, Connector and 'Power or GND').
tools.notes: Saved with EAGLE 6.4 to 7.1 as XML, except Grove-Button-v1.0/Grov-Button-v1.0.sch/.brd (file name 'Grov' as shipped), which are in EAGLE's old binary format; XML tools cannot read those two until EAGLE has opened and saved them.

tools.name: TI MSP430F5529 LaunchPad (MSP-EXP430F5529LP)
tools.description: Schematic and 2-layer board of TI's MSP430F5529 LaunchPad development kit with on-board emulation, full-speed USB, 128 KB flash, 16-channel 12-bit ADC and 20/40-pin BoosterPack headers; about 210 schematic parts. With about 130 board elements it is a good larger test case for CAM and BOM output.
tools.notes: Saved with EAGLE 6.5.

tools.name: Nordic nRF52832 MCU design
tools.description: Schematic and 2-layer board of an nRF52832 Bluetooth Low Energy microcontroller circuit contributed by Nordic Semiconductor (about 55 board elements); complements the Nordic design blocks. Open it together with the Nordic design blocks to compare the reference setups.
tools.example: OPEN nRF52832_MCU.sch   # compare with the Nor_nFR52832-QFAA_* design blocks
tools.notes: Saved with EAGLE 8.3.

tools.name: hexapod example project
tools.description: A consistent schematic/board pair of a hexapod robot controller (about 47 parts). The tutorial folder adds hexapodu.brd, used in the tutorial's net-class and autorouter sections (it contains manually routed signals AC1 and AC2 and restrict rectangles in layers 41/42), and the control file hexapodu.ctl.
tools.notes: cmd-net-list2sch.ulp's usage text uses hexapod.lst as its example net list.

tools.name: bga_example.brd
tools.description: A 4-layer board (layer setup (1*2*15*16)) with about 100 elements around a TFBGA180 device, suited to trying BGA fan-out and escape routing (FANOUT, AUTO BGA) and 4-layer CAM output. It has no schematic.
tools.example:
OPEN bga_example.brd
FANOUT   # click the BGA device
tools.notes: Board only, no schematic.

tools.name: singlesided autorouting example
tools.description: A small schematic/board pair for single-sided autorouting with two autorouter control files, singlesided_h.ctl and singlesided_v.ctl, which differ in the preferred directions of layers 1 and 16; it demonstrates how to set up the autorouter for one-layer boards. Run AUTO with each control file and compare the results.
tools.notes: Compare the results of both control files; RIPUP; between runs.

tools.name: tutorial example files (demo1, demo2, demo3, bus.sch)
tools.description: Files used by the EAGLE tutorial: demo1.sch (a schematic to draw and convert with BOARD), demo2.sch/.brd (consistent pair for forward/back annotation and routing exercises), demo3.sch/.brd (package exchange with PACKAGE/REPLACE), bus.sch (bus handling) plus hexapodu.brd/.ctl for the autorouter chapter. Copy them to your own project folder before working through the tutorial.
tools.example:
OPEN demo1.sch
BOARD   # creates demo1.brd next to it (copy the files to a writable folder first)
tools.notes: The tutorial asks you to copy demo1.sch, demo2.sch and demo2.brd into your own project directory first.

tools.name: stern-dreieck-anlauf.sch (electrical schematic example)
tools.description: Example electrical wiring diagram of a star-delta motor starter (German: Stern-Dreieck-Anlauf) drawn with the elektro libraries: a drawing frame from e-elektro-zeichnungsrahmen, terminals, a motor, a motor protection switch, switches, contactors/relays and fuses. It shows the kind of drawing the elektro libraries and e-*.ulp programs are meant for.
tools.notes: Schematic only (saved with EAGLE 6.0).

tools.name: ngspice simulation example projects
tools.description: The projects\examples\ngspice folder holds simulation-ready schematics with their .simcfg settings, grouped into Analog (convert, curmirror, diode, Fet_Characterization, hierarchy, KVL, mapgates, opamp, oscillator, rcfilter, Sources, switches, xformer), Digital (adder, processing) and MixedMode (gates_and_flops, mixed), plus the model and stimulus files they need. Open any of them and run SIM with the saved settings.
tools.notes: Described entry by entry in the 'SPICE simulation (ngspice)' category.

tools.name: Adafruit design blocks
tools.description: Twelve schematic+board design blocks contributed by Adafruit: 16-channel PWM/servo driver (PCA9685), BMP280 pressure/temperature sensor, Bluefruit LE SPI and USB, Huzzah ESP8266 breakout, PowerBoost 1000C (LiPo charger + boost converter), RGB LCD shield (I2C), TB6612 dual H-bridge, TPA2012 2.1 W class-D amplifier, Trinket 3.3 V and 5 V, and VL6180X time-of-flight sensor. Each contains both a schematic and a board part.
tools.usage: PASTE DBL 'Adafruit/Ada_<name>.dbl' • | Control Panel > Design Blocks > right-click > Add to schematic/board
tools.notes: Files are named Ada_*.dbl in design blocks\examples\Adafruit. With a consistent schematic/board pair open, both halves are pasted.

tools.name: SparkFun design blocks
tools.description: Ten schematic+board design blocks contributed by SparkFun (CC BY-SA 4.0): ESP32 Thing, EasyDriver stepper motor driver, HX711 load-cell amplifier, LSM9DS1 9-axis IMU, basic Micro-USB LiPo charger (500 mA), LilyPad, OpenLog (serial logging to microSD), Venus GPS, XBee Explorer and nRF52832 breakout. Each contains both a schematic and a board part.
tools.notes: Files are named Spk_*.dbl in design blocks\examples\SparkFun.

tools.name: Nordic design blocks
tools.description: Five reference circuits from Nordic Semiconductor as schematic+board blocks: nRF52832 QFAA (QFN48) with DC/DC regulator and NFC, with DC/DC regulator, or with the internal LDO, and nRF51x22 QFAA with DC/DC converter or internal LDO. Each contains both a schematic and a board part.
tools.notes: Nordic's disclaimer in the block description points to nordicsemi.com for the latest reference layout. File names use 'nFR52832' as shipped.

tools.name: Timer design blocks (LM555)
tools.description: Schematic-only design blocks of the LM555 timer in astable (free-running oscillator) and monostable (one-shot pulse) operation. Paste one and adjust the resistor and capacitor values.
tools.notes: Adjust the RC values for the wanted frequency or pulse width.

tools.name: USB to UART design blocks (FT232)
tools.description: Schematic-only FT232-based interfaces: FT232 USB-serial with MAX3233 level translator, USB to MCU UART interface (FT232R), and USB to RS232, RS422 and RS485 converters (FT232R, USB-powered, internal clock). Pick the variant that matches the required interface (TTL UART, RS232, RS422 or RS485).
tools.notes: Quote the path because the folder name contains spaces.

tools.name: LM317M voltage regulator design blocks
tools.description: Schematic-only LM317M (LM317MBSTT3G) positive regulator circuits for fixed 3.3 V, 5 V, 12 V and 24 V outputs and an adjustable-output version. Pick the output voltage you need and check the resistor values against the LM317 data sheet.
tools.notes: Files 3V3-, 5V-, 12V-, 24V- and Adjustable-Voltage-Regulator_LM317M.dbl.

tools.name: MC33063 DC-DC converter design blocks
tools.description: Schematic-only MC33063ADR switching converters in three topologies: step-down (buck), step-up (boost) and voltage-inverting (output of opposite polarity). The block descriptions explain each converter topology.
tools.notes: Recalculate the timing capacitor, inductor and sense resistor for your load.

tools.name: LM386 audio amplifier design blocks
tools.description: Schematic-only LM386M-1 low-voltage audio power amplifiers: one with gain adjustable between 20 and 200, one with the maximum gain of 200. Choose the fixed gain of 200 or the variant with an adjustable gain.
tools.notes: Schematic only; route the board part yourself.

tools.name: ESP8266EX design blocks
tools.description: Schematic-only ESP8266EX Wi-Fi circuits following Espressif's design guidelines: standalone device, slave device (Wi-Fi adapter for another MCU via SPI/SDIO or I2C/UART) and the ESP-LAUNCHER test module. Their descriptions refer to Espressif's design guideline for details.
tools.notes: Follow Espressif's guidelines for the RF layout.

tools.name: Transistor circuit design blocks
tools.description: Schematic-only basic transistor circuits with explanatory descriptions: 2N3904 NPN transistor, Darlington transistor pair, current mirror and constant current source. The block descriptions explain how each circuit works.
tools.notes: For simulation, convert the pasted parts with ADDMODEL first.

tools.name: Helper circuit design blocks (decoupling, jumpers, LED indicators, LDO, 32.768 kHz oscillator)
tools.description: Small reusable sub-circuits: DCPL-VCC and DCPL-VDD decoupling (schematic only), JMP-GND, JMP-VCC and JMP-VDD jumpers, LED-Indicator-DATA and LED-Indicator-VCC, LDO-MCP1703DB-5V0-3V3 (5 V to 3.3 V linear regulator) and Oscillator-32.768K (for nRF parts that need external capacitors); the latter ones include board layout. Paste them to add standard details quickly.
tools.notes: Blocks with a board part keep schematic and board consistent when pasted into a consistent pair.
